cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: decodeQueueLayoutCookie hand-parses a <!DOCTYPE ... [<!ENTITY name SYSTEM "file://...">]> block from an attacker-supplied cookie and reads the referenced file straight off disk via fs.readFileSync, substituting the contents into the document that is then parsed for <column> values and returned to the client. Any authenticated user can set the `escalations_queue_layout` cookie to define a SYSTEM entity pointing at an arbitrary file (e.g. /etc/passwd or a .env with DB credentials / JWT_SECRET) and read its contents back via the `name` attribute in the JSON response. Note the sibling deals/board-layout-cookie.ts explicitly discards any input containing a DOCTYPE, confirming this is a real gap.

extra.message: evaluateCustomForecastFormula compiles and executes an arbitrary attacker-supplied JavaScript expression string (`formula`, only MaxLength(200) validated) via `new Function('context', 'return (' + formula + ');')`. extra.message: The public inviteContinue endpoint redirects to the client-supplied `destination` query parameter with no validation or allowlist (`res.redirect(destination || '/app')`), unlike the adjacent logoutContinue endpoint which whitelists destinations against a fixed list. extra.message: setDisplayName takes `userId` directly from the request body with no check that it matches the authenticated caller and no @Roles restriction, so any authenticated user (including a customer_contact) can rename any other user's account by supplying an arbitrary userId, e.g. an administrator's id.

An attacker can forge an arbitrary/unsigned JWT with any organizationId and be granted a co-view session scoped to that organization's escalation data.
